example.detection_method: Detection leveraged EDR telemetry capturing suspicious PowerShell encoded command execution, anomalous file rename and extension changes on network shares, registry autorun modifications, and network IDS alerts for known ransomware C2 domains with HTTP beaconing patterns. Offline backup validation detected missing recent files. Network segmentation alerts triggered on lateral file share access outside the user baseline.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1059.001 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1547.001 - Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
T1021.002 - Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents the stated cybersecurity problem of Ransomware as a Service (RaaS) in an enterprise context. The scenario describes an affiliate gaining initial access via spear-phishing, deploying a double-extortion ransomware payload with command and control (C2) beaconing, and encrypting critical enterprise file shares, which aligns well with the problem nature. The technical data is comprehensive and realistic, including detailed phishing email headers and body, attachment hashes, SMTP transaction logs, network traffic with DNS queries and C2 beaconing, ransomware payload details including macro code snippet and registry changes, process execution chain, memory dump snippet, and relevant logs such as Windows event logs, file access logs, and IDS alerts. Indicators are clearly listed and correspond to the technical data, supporting the identification of the attack. The detection method explanation ties together EDR telemetry, network IDS alerts, and offline backup validation, reflecting practical risk reduction strategies. Relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques are correctly identified and cover the attack lifecycle stages. Overall, the sample is complete, realistic, and well-aligned with the problem description, providing a strong example for analysis and detection of RaaS attacks in enterprise environments.
